I am 52 this year, and I have only been managing the land myself for about 5 years, so I still mostly follow what works in our village. On my 12 mu, I will keep the wheat-maize double crop. That is the safest for me. We need steady grain, and if one season is not so good, the other can still help. Some people in my family work outside, so labor at home is not always enough. Because of that, I will not do anything too fancy this year. I have well water, but pumping costs money, so I will irrigate when the crop really needs it, not too many times. For fertilizer, I usually do a bit more than the minimum because if wheat or maize shows weak growth later, it is hard to fully recover. But I still have to watch cash, so I will split fertilizer into base and topdressing instead of putting too much at once.

For winter wheat, I will sow in early October, about the usual village timing. I will use a common improved variety that people nearby plant, because saved seed is cheaper but the stand is not always as even. I plan moderate fertilizer: base fertilizer before sowing, then one topdress around jointing if the seedlings look decent. Wheat is worth protecting because it responds well to water and fertilizer here, but I will not push too hard since 12 mu is not large and I do not want input costs to run away. After wheat harvest in June, the turnaround for summer maize is very tight, so I will keep land preparation simple and plant maize quickly. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, apply base fertilizer plus one topdress around the big bell stage, and irrigate only if rain is short. This way, I keep the system familiar, manageable for my family, and not too risky.
